_note: SL-007 IN-M1, closed as its class: a backslash-quote that stands outside a quoted part, which the repair pairs with a later quote or leaves open, joining arguments Windows split. Members come from ordinary input, by accident: a path completed or pasted with its trailing backslash and a closing quote and no opening one, in the root, the report path, or both; a line that ends with a quote; two such paths in one line. 'tail' is the command line after the program's name as typed, 'windows' is what Windows' own splitter makes of it (checked by the test, shell32), and 'expect' says what CommandLine.Arguments does with it: 'repaired' (the arguments as typed, in 'result', which is the repair doing its job and must keep doing it), 'kept' (Windows' split as it is: only the root's trailing quote is damaged, which RootArgument repairs), or 'refused' (null: Windows merged arguments that nothing can take apart). 'before' says what the code did without the pairing and exposed-token steps, kept so that the rows the fix closed stay shown. UnpairedQuoteCorpusTests runs every row, then runs a sweep over every line made of up to four of a set of tokens and holds four properties of the whole class: no option Windows exposed is hidden, a repair never leaves a quote open, an exposed root is never joined, and null is only for arguments Windows merged.

dashSweep._note: SL-007 O-053, closed as its class: path pieces that start with two dashes after a space, which Windows exposes as tokens of their own. The app has one option, --report, so only that spelling may ever be told from a piece of a path. 'rename' is the pair the test applies to every line (and to the repair's answer): a name's dashes are never the reason for a different verdict. The tokens are the shapes a dashed piece reaches the repair in: alone, as the tail of a quoted path, with a trailing quote, beside a root with a backslash-quote, beside --report.
